subject: A thought about next week's check-in
text:
I hope it is alright to mention this so casually, but after checking my notes from Tuesday I realised I may have misread the calendar entry for the project check-in. The invitation appeared to show Wednesday at four, yet the agenda link now opens a Thursday morning slot, which has thrown my preparation into slight disorder.

I do not want to make a fuss, because these things happen to everyone, especially when several meetings are packed into the same week. I simply want to let you know that if Thursday is correct, I can attend and speak briefly about the budget tracker. If Wednesday remains the intended date, I would need a little extra time to finish the supplier comparison.

The small piece of advice I would offer is to send a short calendar update with the revised time in the subject line. I know from experience that people often assume the attached agenda carries all the details, so a brief sentence such as 'moved to Thursday, 10:00' could quietly prevent more confusion. It also helps when a student has to rearrange classes, because we tend to scan quickly rather than read every note. If it helps, I can forward the revised summary beforehand, so the discussion feels less rushed. That may save a few minutes. I do not want to overcomplicate it.

Thank you for your patience with my uncertainty. I am happy to work around whatever timing you prefer, and I will follow up after you confirm.
